title_en: Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Medical Damage Liability Dispute Cases

articles.content_en:
Article 1: This Interpretation shall apply to cases where a patient, on the grounds of suffering personal injury or property damage during diagnosis and treatment activities, requests a medical institution, the producer, seller, drug marketing authorization holder, or blood supply institution to bear tort liability.
This Interpretation shall apply to tort dispute cases filed by a patient on the grounds of suffering personal injury or property damage during medical beauty activities carried out in a medical beauty institution or a medical institution that has set up a medical beauty department.
This Interpretation shall not apply to medical service contract dispute cases filed by the parties.

Article 2: Where a patient suffers damage after receiving diagnosis and treatment in multiple medical institutions for the same illness or injury, and prosecutes some or all of the medical institutions where he or she sought treatment, the case shall be accepted.
Where a patient prosecutes some of the medical institutions where he or she sought treatment, and thereafter a party applies according to law to add other medical institutions where treatment was sought as co-defendants or third parties, such application shall be permitted. Where necessary, the People's Court may according to law add relevant parties to participate in the proceedings.

Article 3: Where a patient suffers damage due to a defective medical product and prosecutes some or all of the producers, sellers, drug marketing authorization holders, and medical institutions, the case shall be accepted.
Where a patient only prosecutes some of the subjects among the producers, sellers, drug marketing authorization holders, and medical institutions, and a party applies according to law to add other subjects as co-defendants or third parties, such application shall be permitted. Where necessary, the People's Court may according to law add relevant parties to participate in the proceedings.
Where a patient brings a tort action for damage caused by the input of substandard blood, the preceding two paragraphs shall apply mutatis mutandis.

Article 4: Where a patient claims that a medical institution shall bear compensation liability pursuant to Article 1218 of the Civil Code, he or she shall submit evidence of having sought treatment at that medical institution and of suffering damage.
Where a patient is unable to submit evidence that the medical institution or its medical personnel was at fault or that there is a causal relationship between the diagnosis and treatment behavior and the damage, and he or she applies according to law for medical damage expert evaluation, the People's Court shall permit it.
Where a medical institution claims that it shall not bear liability, it shall bear the burden of proof with respect to defensive matters such as the circumstances provided in the first paragraph of Article 1224 of the Civil Code.

Article 5: Where a patient claims that a medical institution shall bear compensation liability pursuant to Article 1219 of the Civil Code, he or she shall submit evidence in accordance with the provisions of the first paragraph of the preceding article.
Where surgery, special examination, or special treatment is performed, the medical institution shall bear the obligation of explanation and obtain explicit consent from the patient or the patient's close relatives, except in circumstances falling under Article 1220 of the Civil Code. Where the medical institution submits evidence of explicit consent from the patient or the patient's close relatives, the People's Court may determine that the medical institution has fulfilled its explanation obligation, except where the patient has contrary evidence sufficient to rebut it.

Article 6: The medical record materials provided in Article 1222 of the Civil Code include outpatient medical records, hospitalization records, temperature sheets, medical order sheets, laboratory test reports, medical imaging examination materials, special examination (treatment) consent forms, surgical consent forms, surgical and anesthesia records, pathological materials, nursing records, discharge records, and other medical record materials prescribed by the health administrative department of the State Council.
Where a patient applies to the People's Court according to law for a medical institution to submit medical record materials related to the dispute that are kept by it, and the medical institution fails to submit them within the time limit designated by the People's Court, the People's Court may presume that the medical institution is at fault in accordance with item (2) of Article 1222 of the Civil Code, except where it is unable to submit them due to objective reasons such as force majeure.

Article 7: Where a patient claims compensation pursuant to Article 1223 of the Civil Code, he or she shall submit evidence of using a medical product or receiving a blood transfusion and of suffering damage.
Where a patient is unable to submit evidence of a causal relationship between the use of a medical product or the blood transfusion and the damage, and he or she applies for expert evaluation according to law, the People's Court shall permit it.
Where a medical institution, the producer, seller, drug marketing authorization holder, or blood supply institution claims that it shall not bear liability, it shall bear the burden of proof with respect to defensive matters such as the absence of defects in the medical product or the conformity of the blood.

Article 8: Where a party applies according to law for expert evaluation of a specialized issue in a medical damage liability dispute, the People's Court shall permit it.
Where a party fails to apply for expert evaluation, and the People's Court considers that the specialized issue provided in the preceding paragraph requires evaluation, the People's Court shall commission an expert evaluation ex officio.

Article 9: Where a party applies for medical damage expert evaluation, the experts shall be determined through consultation between the parties.
Where the parties cannot reach an agreement on the expert, and the People's Court proposes a method for determining the expert, if the parties agree, the expert shall be determined in accordance with that method; if the parties do not agree, the expert shall be designated by the People's Court.
The expert shall be determined from among experts who have corresponding appraisal capability and meet the appraisal requirements.

Article 10: Where a medical damage expert evaluation is commissioned, the parties shall submit true, complete, and sufficient evaluation materials as required. If the submitted evaluation materials do not meet the requirements, the People's Court shall notify the parties to replace or supplement the corresponding materials.
Before commissioning the expert evaluation, the People's Court shall organize the parties to cross-examine the evaluation materials.

Article 12: The expert evaluation opinion may express the degree of causative potency of the diagnosis and treatment behavior or medical product in causing the patient's damage according to whether it is the entire cause, primary cause, equal cause, secondary cause, minor cause, or no causal relationship with the patient's damage.

Article 13: An expert evaluation opinion shall be cross-examined by the parties.
Where a party applies for the expert to appear in court to testify, and the People's Court examines and approves it, or the People's Court considers it necessary for the expert to appear in court, the People's Court shall notify the expert to appear in court to testify. Where both parties agree that the expert may testify by means of written explanations, audio-visual transmission technology, or audio-visual materials, such testimony may be permitted.
Where the expert cannot appear in court on time due to health reasons, natural disasters, other force majeure, or other legitimate reasons, the court session may be postponed; with the permission of the People's Court, the expert may also testify by means of written explanations, audio-visual transmission technology, or audio-visual materials.
Where the expert refuses to appear in court to testify without the reasons provided in the preceding paragraph, and the party does not accept the evaluation opinion, the evaluation opinion shall not be admitted.

Article 14: Where a party applies for notifying one or two persons with specialized medical knowledge to appear in court to give opinions on the expert evaluation opinion or other specialized factual issues of the case, and the People's Court permits it, the persons with specialized medical knowledge shall be notified to appear in court.
The opinions given by the persons with specialized medical knowledge provided in the preceding paragraph shall be regarded as statements of the party and, after cross-examination, may serve as the basis for determining the facts of the case.

Article 15: Where a party commissions an expert on its own to make a medical damage evaluation opinion, and the other party recognizes it, the opinion may be admitted.
Where the parties jointly commission an expert to make a medical damage evaluation opinion, if one party does not recognize it, that party shall put forward specific objections and reasons. Upon examination, if there is evidence sufficient to establish that the objection is justified, the evaluation opinion shall not be admitted; if the objection is not justified, the evaluation opinion shall be admitted.

Article 16: The fault of a medical institution or its medical personnel shall be determined in accordance with laws, administrative regulations, rules, and other relevant diagnosis and treatment norms, and factors such as the urgency of the patient's condition, individual differences of the patient, the local medical level, and the qualifications of the medical institution and medical personnel may be comprehensively considered.

Article 17: Where medical personnel violate the obligation provided in the first paragraph of Article 1219 of the Civil Code, but do not cause personal injury to the patient, and the patient requests the medical institution to bear liability for damages, such request shall not be supported.

Article 19: Where the diagnosis and treatment behaviors of two or more medical institutions cause the same damage to a patient, and the patient requests the medical institutions to bear compensation liability, the compensation liability to be borne by each medical institution shall be determined by distinguishing different circumstances and in accordance with Article 1168, Article 1171, or Article 1172 of the Civil Code.

Article 20: Where a medical institution invites medical personnel outside the institution to provide diagnosis and treatment to a patient, and the patient suffers damage due to the fault of the invited medical personnel, the inviting medical institution shall bear compensation liability.

Article 21: Where a patient suffers damage due to a defect in a medical product or the input of substandard blood, and requests the medical institution, the producer, seller, drug marketing authorization holder of the defective medical product, or the blood supply institution to bear compensation liability, such request shall be supported.
Where a medical institution, after bearing compensation liability, seeks recourse against the producer, seller, drug marketing authorization holder of the defective medical product, or the blood supply institution, such claim shall be supported.
Where, due to the fault of a medical institution, a medical product has defects or blood is substandard, and the producer, seller, drug marketing authorization holder, or blood supply institution, after bearing compensation liability, seeks recourse against the medical institution, such claim shall be supported.

Article 22: Where a defective medical product and the faulty diagnosis and treatment behavior of a medical institution jointly cause the same damage to a patient, and the patient requests the medical institution and the producer, seller, drug marketing authorization holder of the medical product to bear joint and several liability, such request shall be supported.
Where a medical institution or the producer, seller, drug marketing authorization holder of a medical product, after bearing compensation liability, seeks recourse against other liable subjects, the corresponding amount shall be determined according to the degree of causative potency of the diagnosis and treatment behavior and the defective medical product in causing the patient's damage.
Where the input of substandard blood and the faulty diagnosis and treatment behavior of a medical institution jointly cause the same damage to a patient, the preceding two paragraphs shall apply mutatis mutandis.

Article 23: Where the producer, seller, or drug marketing authorization holder of a medical product, knowing that the medical product has defects, still produces or sells it, causing the patient's death or severe damage to health, and the infringed party requests the producer, seller, or drug marketing authorization holder to compensate losses and punitive damages of not more than twice the amount, the People's Court shall support such request.

Article 25: Where, after the death of a patient, his or her close relatives request compensation for medical damage, this Interpretation shall apply; where a person who paid reasonable expenses such as the patient's medical expenses and funeral expenses requests compensation for such expenses, this Interpretation shall apply.
The "medical products" mentioned in this Interpretation include drugs, disinfection products, medical devices, and the like.

Article 26: Where any judicial interpretation previously issued by this Court is inconsistent with this Interpretation, this Interpretation shall prevail.
Where a case has not yet become final after this Interpretation comes into force, this Interpretation shall apply; where a case has already become final before this Interpretation comes into force, and a party applies for retrial or a decision is made to retry the case in accordance with the trial supervision procedure, this Interpretation shall not apply.
